title: The high school band Lawson led, Nat Cole and Nat Towles
summary: Helen Dance asks whether he knew the Booker T. Washington band that Nat Cole or Nat Towles fronted; he might have heard it without knowing.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington High School band

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, now, T-Bone told me that Christian took his place with the band, he was with.

Yeah. They called him in, and Lawson fell out with the man that owned the dance hall, which was upstairs. Somewhere on Central Avenue, it was up above a cafe. I've forgotten, the name will come to me. But, anyway, so then they sent for the piano player, singer, that died? Nat Cole.
And Nat Cole took over the band. That still doesn't tell you what that band was. It was the high school band. It was the Booker T. Washington high school band.
Oh, I don't know, I'm not so sure where
Nat was from. They got him from, like, Arkansas or Louisiana or something like that. They sent for him from somewhere. This would be before -- even before he had the trio and all that.
But I just -- the reason I mentioned it to you, I'm just trying to see it if tied up so you'd ever had heard of that band.
I might have heard it and didn't know it.
It's like Boots and his Buddies and --
Well, that's right, yes, because they were Dallas, weren't they?
They came out of Dallas, didn't they?
They came from out of the South, but not Dallas.
San Antonio, Texas, it could have been.
Let's see, who's in San Antonio now? What's the guy's name, he used to have a good band.
He has a club there. He did.
Oh, I was thinking maybe Gene had mentioned him, but I don't think he did. Ramey. We're just about going to go, aren't we?
Well, that really is beside the point. The only reason I'm bringing them up is to see where the background T-Bone was and everything. So let's get back to the fact that you --
